PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Makes Rooftop Solar Accessible for All with Subsidy Support and Low-Interest Financing
articles.full_content:
In order to ensure the affordability of rooftop solar (RTS) systems for middle-income and economically weaker households under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY), following provisions have been made:
• Higher central financial assistance for the first two kWp of RTS capacity.
• Availability of collateral-free loan from nationalized banks at a concessional interest rate of repo-rate plus 50 bps, i.e., 5.75% per annum for the present, with a tenure of 10 years.
• Included RESCO/Utility-Led Aggregation (ULA) Models.

While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 households reported even zero electricity bills for some months, depending on their self-consumption of electricity.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

articles.title: Centre Promotes Convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar Schemes to Accelerate Solar Adoption and Rural Energy Self-Sufficiency
articles.full_content:
Government has been promoting convergence of PM KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana with suitable Central and State programmes and funding sources, wherever feasible, to facilitate wider adoption of the schemes. For instance, PM KUSUM scheme guidelines allow for convergence with other central schemes including:
• Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) scheme for access of easy financing
• Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) for solarization of segregated agriculture feeders
• Promotion of micro irrigation techniques and Per Drop More Crop scheme
• Replacement of agriculture pumps with energy efficient pumps
• Gram Urja Swaraj Campaign to enhance self-sufficiency at village level
Similarly for PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, the convergence is taken up with Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), for implementing the Solar Didi Programme under which women Self-Help Group (SHG) members under DAY-NULM are trained. Convergence of District Mineral Foundation (DMF) funds is also encouraged with PM Surya Ghar for eligible beneficiaries, particularly BPL households, PMAY beneficiaries and other vulnerable sections.
The Ministry has already issued communications and possible areas of convergence to all the states for convergence of PM KUSUM and PMSG Schemes with scheme of Ministry of Cooperation, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Rural Development etc.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

articles.title: Over 48 Lakh Households Benefit Under PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana Since February 2024
articles.full_content:
The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (PMSG: MBY) is a demand-driven scheme wherein all residential consumers in the country including the rural households, having a grid-connected electricity connection with the local DISCOM, can avail the benefits of the scheme, for installation of rooftop solar (RTS) systems by applying on the National Portal ( www.pmsuryaghar.gov.in ) of the scheme.
During the year 2025-26, a total of 18. 71 lakh RTS systems have been installed with a cumulative installed solar capacity of 6.7 GW, benefitting 22.71 lakh households across the country, including the rural households under the PMSG: MBY.
Under the PMSG: MBY, since its launch in February 2024, a total of 39,72,447 RTS systems have been installed, benefitting 48,02,717 households across the country including the households in rural areas, as on 22.07.2026.
While the electricity bills of consumers installed RTS under the scheme have been largely reduced, over 18.93 lakh beneficiaries have been reported by DISCOMs across the country , including the rural households to receive zero electricity bill after installation of RTS systems under the scheme during the any month/billing period , depending on their self-consumption of electricity.
Apart from installation of rooftop solar plants in residential sector, the PMSG: MBY also envisage installation of RTS plants in Government and commercial buildings including educational and health institutions, however, no central financial assistance (CFA) is provided to these categories of consumers as installation of rooftop solar plants is financially viable for them even without CFA.
This information was submitted by the Union Minister of State for Ministry of New & Renewable Energy, Shri Shripad Yesso Naik in a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha.

articles.full_content:
The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles is being implemented by the Ministry of Textiles across the country to promote the production of MMF Apparel, MMF Fabrics and products of Technical Textiles. The Scheme is aimed at promoting investment, enhancing manufacturing capacities, improving competitiveness of the textile sector and encouraging value addition in the identified product segments. The implementation of the Scheme is monitored and reviewed periodically at various levels in the Ministry. Further, weekly Open House sessions and monthly workshops are organized with the beneficiary companies to facilitate implementation of the Scheme and to resolve issues, if any, relating to project execution. The Ministry also organizes outreach-cum-knowledge sessions in various States, including Maharashtra, to create awareness about the Scheme and facilitate stakeholder participation.
Under the Production Linked Incentive scheme (PLI) for Textiles, a total of 170 companies have been approved across India of which 24 companies pertain to Maharashtra. As of March 31, 2026, investment to the tune of ₹167.51 crores have been made by these companies in Maharashtra. District-wise details are given below.
To make the PLI Scheme more attractive for the prospective investors in the MMF and Technical Textiles sector, the Scheme has been modified in October, 2025, with key revisions such as Expansion of Eligible Notified Products by addition of 17 new HSN codes in MMF Apparel and Fabrics, Relaxation from setting up new companies to avail benefit of the Scheme, Reduction in minimum threshold criteria of investment by 50% and Reduction in incremental turnover Criteria for incentive from earlier 25% to 10%. To create comprehensive awareness and participation, the Ministry has proactively engaged with all major textile industry associations to disseminate information regarding the recent revisions in the Scheme and had also reopened the application portal of the Scheme till 31.03.2026 to accept new applications. As a result of this revision, MSME participation has increased significantly with 65 of the 96 applications received under Round 3 of the Scheme (approximately 68%) pertaining to the MSME sector.

articles.full_content:
Madras Fertilizers Limited, RO - Hyderabad successfully organized “Kisan Sangoshthi : PM PRANAM” programme at Rythuvedika, Vemulapally Mandal, Nalgonda District today. The programme was organized by Shri S.Karuppaiah, Manager-Marketing, Telangana State, MFL with the support and guidance of Shri Chandra Sekar, Regional Manager and Shri Umashankar, CMM, MFL RO-Hyderabad. Dignitaries & Participation The event was graced by: 1. Shri Jagadesh Reddy, ADA, Miryalaguda 2. Shri Kishore Naik, AO 3. Shri Shafi, AEO 4. Shri http://S.Karuppaiah, Manager-Marketing, MFL Telangana State A total of ∼45 farmers participated in the programme. 23 Women Farmers took active part in the discussions. Key Highlights 1. MFL Role & Products: Shri http://S.Karuppaiah, Manager-Marketing explained about MFL and its role in supporting farmers. He detailed about VIJAY Brand fertilizers, Organic Manure, City Compost and other alternate nutrients. 2. PM-PRANAM Scheme: Farmers were educated on "Promotion of Alternate Nutrients for Agriculture Management". The need to reduce chemical fertilizer usage and promote soil health was explained. 3. Govt Vision: The Govt of India's focus on Organic Manure usage and Balanced Fertilizer Application for sustainable agriculture was highlighted. 4. ADA Address: Shri Jagadesh Reddy, ADA explained about Govt schemes, soil testing importance, and balanced fertilizer use. 5. VIJAY Organic Manures: Shri Kishore Naik, AO spoke about the benefits of VIJAY Organic Manures and organic inputs for better yield and soil fertility. 6. Farmer Grievances: Farmers expressed concerns about season failure and difficulties they are facing currently in agriculture. Officials assured all possible support and guidance. 7. Farmer Interaction: Shri Shafi, AEO clarified farmer doubts on crop practices. MFL team explained the benefits of VIJAY Brand fertilizers. 8. An interactive session was held where women farmers raised queries on crop nutrition and subsidies. All doubts were clarified. 9. Literature and pamphlets on PM PRANAM, City Compost and Organic Manures were distributed to all farmers.
Arrangements For farmer convenience, snacks, cooling drinks, water and biscuits were provided. Banner and Standee on PM PRANAM Scheme and VIJAY Brand were displayed for wider publicity. Outcome The programme received an excellent response. Farmers, especially women farmers, assured to adopt balanced fertilizer practices and increase the use of organic manures and city compost. The guidance from ADA, AO & AEO motivated the farming community. The objective of “Kisan Sangoshthi : PM PRANAM” was achieved successfully with good participation under the leadership of Shri Chandra Sekar, RM and Shri Umashankar, CMM. articles.full_content:
Toy Biz International 2026 Showcases 400 Indian Brands, Boosting Domestic Sales and Export Opportunities Government Initiatives Boost Quality, Safety and Competitiveness of India's Toy Industry
The 17th Toy Biz International B2B Exhibition was organized by the Toy Association of India from 4th to 7th July, 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The Exhibition aimed at promoting Indian toys, facilitating business networking, and creating opportunities for growth in domestic sales and exports. It witnessed participation of 400 Indian toy brands, 100 international buyers from 40 countries, and around 30,000 business visitors. The exhibition provided platform for connecting manufacturers with wholesalers, retailers, distributors, institutional buyers and e-commerce platforms.
At present, there is no dedicated toy policy of the Government of India.
In 2018-19, Toys worth USD 371.7 Mn were imported into India. A large proportion of these toys were unsafe, substandard, counterfeit, and cheap. Further, a Mystery Shopping exercise conducted in 2019 revealed that only 33% toys in the domestic market were of acceptable quality as per BIS standards.
In order to improve the quality and safety of toys in the country and to promote the overall development of the Indian toy industry, the Government of India has undertaken several initiatives. The key initiatives are as follows:
• Formulation of a comprehensive National Action Plan for Toys (NAPT), comprising 21 action points and coordinated by 14 Ministries and Departments. It focuses on promoting the design and development of toys based on Indian values, culture, and history; encouraging the use of toys as learning resources; organizing hackathons, toy fairs, and grand challenges for toy design and manufacturing; strengthening quality monitoring and restricting the import of substandard and unsafe toys; promoting indigenous toy clusters; and boosting domestic manufacturing.
• Basic Custom Duty (BCD) on Toys (HS Code-9503) was increased from 20% to 60% in February 2020, and subsequently increased to 70% in 2023. Further, the BCD on Parts of Electronic Toys (HS 95030091) revised as 20% in the Budget F.Y. 2025-26.
• A Quality Control Order (QCO) for Toys was issued on 25.02.2020, implemented with effect from 01.01.2021.
• BIS has granted more than 1800 licenses to domestic manufacturers of toys and more than 50 licenses to foreign manufacturers for use of BIS Standard Mark on toys conforming to the Indian Standards for safety of toys.
• The National Education Policy 2020 formulated by Ministry of Education focuses on play and activity-based learning. A handbook on ‘Toy Based Pedagogy’ has been published by NCERT with the objective of ensuring that the learning process for children is enjoyable and fun. It prescribes toys, especially based on indigenous toys and games to be used at different stages to help develop many competencies in young children.

India's Index of industrial production records growth of 7.3% in June 2026
articles.full_content:
Quick Estimates of Index of Industrial Production and Use- Based Index for the Month of June 2026 (Base 2022-23=100)
In June 2026, Index of Industrial Production recorded a 7.3% year-on-year growth, supported by 7.8% growth in Manufacturing sector and strong growth of 10.6% in Electricity & Gas Supply sector.
The Quick Estimate of Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is released on 28 th of every month (or next working day if 28 th is a holiday). The index is compiled with data received from source agencies, which in turn receive the data from the producing factories/ establishments. These Quick Estimates will undergo revision in subsequent releases as per the revision policy of IIP.
2. Key Highlights:
• The IIP growth rate for the month of June 2026 is 7.3 percent which was 5.1 percent (Quick Estimate) in the month of May 2026.
• The growth rates of the sectors, Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 are 1.0 percent, 7.8 percent, 10.6 percent and 6.1 percent respectively.
• The Quick Estimate of IIP stands at 123.1 against 114.7 in June 2025. The indices of Industrial Production for Mining & Quarrying, Manufacturing, Electricity & Gas Supply and Water Supply, Sewerage & Waste Management for the month of June 2026 stand at 110.0, 123.3, 131.0 and 145.7 respectively.
• Within the Manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industry groups at NIC 2 digit-level have recorded a positive growth in June 2026 over June 2025. The top three positive contributors for the month of June 2026 are – “Manufacture of electrical equipment” (34.0%), “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers” (17.5%), and “Manufacture of food products” (10.8%).
• In the industry group “Manufacture of electrical equipment” item groups “Electrical Apparatus for Switching or Protecting Electrical Circuits (e.g., Switchgear, Circuit Breakers/Switches, Control/Meter Panels) and Parts Thereof”, “UPS and Solid-State Drives”, and “End-Face Connectors for Optical Fibres and Cables” have shown significant contribution in growth.
• In the industry group “Manufacture of motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers”, item groups “Auto Components, Spares and Accessories”, “Passenger Cars”, and “Commercial Vehicles” have shown significant contribution in growth.
• In the industry group “Manufacture of food products”, item groups “Tea”, “Rice (Other Than Basmati)”, and “Starch, All Types” have shown significant contribution in growth.
• As per the Use-Based Classification, the indices stand at 119.5 for Primary Goods, 140.5 for Capital Goods, 124.2 for Intermediate Goods and 132.9 for Infrastructure/ Construction Goods for the month of June 2026. Further, the indices for Consumer durables and Consumer non-durables stand at 119.8 and 115.4 respectively.

Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto)
articles.full_content:
The following schemes are administered by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to promote domestic manufacturing and technological upgradation:
(i) Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India (PLI-Auto): The Government approved this scheme on 23.09.2021 for Automobile and Auto Component Industry in India for enhancing India's manufacturing capabilities for Advanced Automotive Technology (AAT) products with a budgetary outlay of Rs. 25,938 crore. The scheme provides financial incentives on manufacturing of AAT products including EVs with minimum 50% Domestic Value Addition (DVA) and attract investments in the automotive manufacturing value chain. The Scheme has attracted an investment of Rs. 44,326 Crore and generated employment of 67,820 till 31.03.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects.
(ii) Production Linked Incentive Scheme on National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage: The Government on 12.05.2021 approved PLI Scheme for manufacturing of ACC in the country with a budgetary outlay of Rs.18,100 crore. The scheme aims to establish a competitive domestic manufacturing ecosystem for 50 GWh of ACC batteries, out of which 40 GWh ACC capacity has been awarded to four beneficiary firms. Under the Scheme, a Giga-Scale ACC manufacturing plant with an installed capacity of 1.4 GWh has been established. The scheme has attracted an investment of ₹5,180 crore and direct employment of 1,277 till 31.05.2026. Further, under the Scheme, expenditures incurred by beneficiary firms on Research and Development (R&D) are permitted to meet investment criteria, allowing them to integrate the latest technology in the implementation of their projects.
(iii) PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme: This scheme has been approved with an outlay of Rs. 10,900 crore w.e.f. 01.04.2024 till 31.03.2028. The scheme supports domestic manufacturing of electric vehicles including e-2W, e-3W, e-Trucks, e-buses and e-Ambulances. The scheme also supports EV public charging stations and upgradation of testing agencies.
(iv) Scheme on Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector- Phase-II: This Scheme has the objective to encourage technology development and strengthen domestic manufacturing capabilities. articles.full_content:
The vision of a drug free Tamil Nadu can be achieved only through awareness: Superintendent of Police, Ramananathapuram District
Shri M. Sivaguru Prabhakaran, District Collector, Ramanathapuram, said that Media plays a major role in taking the government welfare measures to the beneficiaries. He said this while presiding over an orientation program for journalists, organized by the Press Information Bureau, Chennai at Ramanathapuram today. The programme aimed at strengthening responsible journalism, enhancing awareness on government initiatives and equipping media professionals with the knowledge to effectively counter misinformation in the digital age.
Speaking at the event, Shri Sivaguru Prabhakaran described the media as the fourth pillar of democracy and appreciated its constructive role in governance. He said several district administration initiatives had been strengthened through proactive media support. Such orientation programmes, help journalists upgrade their knowledge and professional skills.
Shri G. Chandeesh, Superintendent of Police, Ramanathapuram, enlightened the journalists on the importance of effective communication and highlighted the crucial role of the media in ensuring accurate dissemination of information relating to police and government initiatives. Reiterating the vision of a Drug-Free Tamil Nadu, he emphasised that awareness among the public, especially parents and youth, is essential to eliminate drug abuse.
Delivering the keynote address, Shri V. Palanichamy, Director General (i/c) South Zone, Press Information Bureau, underscored the importance of accuracy, brevity and clarity in journalism. He said the media today faces two major challenges—AI-generated content and fake news and the rapid evolution of technology. He urged journalists to uphold professional ethics while embracing technological advancements. He also called upon the media to provide greater coverage to government welfare and developmental initiatives so that their benefits reach the intended beneficiaries.
In a special session, Shri P. Arun Kumar, Director, Press Information Bureau, Chennai, delivered an interactive presentation on misinformation and disinformation. He explained practical methods of verifying digital content, identifying manipulated information and using fact-checking tools to ensure responsible journalism.
During the technical session on Sustainable Fisheries and Blue Economy, Dr. Vikas P.A., Senior Scientist, ICAR-Central Marine Fisheries Research Institute (CMFRI), Mandapam, Ramanathapuram highlighted the vast potential of seaweed cultivation and cage fish farming in improving the livelihoods of coastal communities. He spoke about the Government's continued support for fisheries research and sustainable aquaculture and outlined various initiatives under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), including a Central Government contribution of Rs.9,407 crore for fisheries development.

articles.full_content:
From 16.71% to 82.09%: Jal Jeevan Mission Transforming Rural Tap Water Coverage 15.89 Crore Rural Households Connected to Functional Household Tap Connections Under JJM
To enable every rural household in the country to have assured potable water, in adequate quantity ( 55 litres per capita per day ) of prescribed quality ( BIS:10500 ) on regular and long-term basis, through tap water connection, since August 2019, Government of India in partnership with states, has been implementing Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) - Har Ghar Jal.
'Jal Arpan' is being organized as a community-led public event with active participation of elected representatives, Gram Sabhas and local communities to celebrate successful commissioning of water supply schemes and promote long-term sustainability of rural water infrastructure. To promote Jan Bhagidari for sustainable and continuous service delivery under the JJM, a standardized “ Handbook on Community-Managed Piped Water Systems ” has been launched under the Jal Arpan initiative. The handbook mandates a 15-day trial run involving Gram Panchayats (GPs)/ Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSCs)/ Pani Samiti members to ensure smooth handover of water supply schemes and sustainable operations.
Significant progress has been made in the country since the launch of JJM towards enhancing access to tap water to rural households. At the time of announcement of Jal Jeevan Mission, 3.23 Crore (16.71%) rural households were reported to have tap water connections. So far, as reported by States/ UTs as on 18.07.2026, around 12.66 Crore additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 18.07.2026, out of 19.36 Crore rural households, in the country, around 15.89 Crore (82.09%) households are reported to have tap water supply in their homes. State/ UT-wise details are at Annex .
‘Drinking Water’ is a state subject, and hence, the responsibility of planning, approval, implementation, operation and maintenance (O&M) of drinking water supply schemes, including those under the JJM, lies with State/ UT Governments. The Government of India supports the states by providing technical and financial assistance. All States/ UTs have been advised to notify comprehensive Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Policy in place with provisions for handing over of schemes to GPs/ VWSCs, empowering them to levy user charges, engaging women Self Help Groups (SHGs) for the collection of user charges, and undertaking O&M, and ensuring sufficient financing of O&M. The details of Gram Panchayat level collection of user charges are not maintained at Government of India level.
In March 2026, the Union Cabinet has approved the extension of JJM period up to December 2028 with enhanced outlay and restructured implementation focusing on structural reforms in rural drinking water supply sector under JJM 2.0.

STREET VENDORS UNDER PM SVANIDHI
articles.full_content:
PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) scheme was launched on 01 st June 2020. Under the scheme, till 12 th July 2026, 76.95 lakhs street vendor have availed 1.15 crore loans amounting to ₹18475.06 Crore. Under the scheme, working capital term loans are provided to the street vendors in three tranches of upto ₹15,000, ₹25,000, and ₹50,000 to be repaid in 12 months, 18 months, and 36 months respectively through monthly instalments. Therefore, repayment varies accordingly.State-wise details are available on PM SVANidhi portal https://pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in
Since scheme inception till 12 th July 2026, the number of street vendors who have availed the second and third tranches of loans under the scheme are 29,71,195 and 8,49,471 respectively.
SVANidhi se Samriddhi’ component under the PM SVANidhi Scheme, was launched on 04 January, 2021, to build social security net for the beneficiaries’ families for improving their living conditions. This facilitates linkages to 8 select Central Government Welfare schemes designed to provide a safety net and social security for the eligible beneficiaries and their families. As on 12th July 2026, socio economic profiling is completed for 50.63 lakh PM SVANidhi beneficiaries along with 1.06 crore family members and a total of 1.56 crore scheme sanctions have been extended to them.
Impact assessment studies of the PM SVANidhi scheme was undertaken by Indian School of Business (ISB), Hyderabad in 2023 & 2025. The 2023 study was conducted in 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries and it found that PM SVANidhi was the first loan from a bank for 95% of the beneficiaries and the loan was utilized for expanding their business. The 2025 study was conducted in 99 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) across the country covering more than 5,000 beneficiaries (with around 60% of the respondents being part of the 2023 study sample) and it found that the average annualized business income among SVANidhi borrowers grew by around 20 percent, between 2023 and 2025.
Around 30 percent of borrowers across all cycles reported holding loans other than PM SVANidhi loans which underscores the scheme’s role in building credit histories for vendors who previously had little or no access to formal credit. Further the study also found that between 2023 and 2025, the adoption of digital payments among street vendors rose significantly.
The study also found the scheme’s impact extends well beyond business recovery. By easing credit constraints and stabilizing household cash flows, the scheme has enabled vendor families to improve living conditions, strengthen food security, enhance access to health-care, and support children’s education.
This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today.

articles.full_content:
The National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), convened a meeting with Skill Universities at Kaushal Bhawan, New Delhi, under the chairpersonship of Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, MSDE and Chairperson, NCVET, to deliberate on strengthening India's vocational education ecosystem through enhanced collaboration, quality assurance and policy convergence. The meeting was graced by Shri N. K. Sudhanshu, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Executive Member, NCVET. The meeting was also attended by Prof. (Dr.) Ashok Kumar Gaba, Executive Member, NCVET; Ms. ArchanaMayaram, Economic Advisor, MSDE; Lt. Col. Vikram Singh Bhati, Director, NCVET; and Lt. Col. Saurabh S. Bisht, Director, NCVET.
The consultation brought together more than 25 senior academic leaders representing 14 Skill Universities across 10 States and one Union Territory, including Delhi Skill and Entrepreneurship University (DSEU), Symbiosis Skills and Professional University (SSPU), Medhavi Skills University, Shri Vishwakarma Skill University (SVSU), Ratan Tata Maharashtra State Skills University, Assam Skill University, Kaushalya – The Skill University, Young India Skills University, Bhartiya Skill Development University (BSDU), Scope Global Skills University, Centurion University of Technology and Management (CUTM), Sikkim Skill University, Lamrin Tech Skills University, and Vishvakarma Skills University, Jaipur (VSURAJ). The consultation provided a platform for deliberations on strengthening institutional collaboration, enhancing quality assurance and advancing the implementation of vocational education reforms across the country.
The meeting was organised in furtherance of the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, which envisages seamless integration of vocational education with general and higher education, enhanced learner mobility, multiple pathways for progression and lifelong learning opportunities.
In her inaugural address, Smt. Debashree Mukherjee emphasised the pivotal role of Skill Universities in preparing a future-ready workforce and highlighted NCVET's commitment to fostering a robust, transparent and outcome-oriented regulatory ecosystem. She underlined the importance of closer institutional collaboration for promoting quality assurance, innovation and wider adoption of the National Skills Qualification Framework (NSQF) across the higher education landscape.
The participating universities made presentations on their institutional profiles, vocational education initiatives, innovative models of skill delivery, industry engagement practices and implementation experiences. They also highlighted regulatory and operational challenges and offered suggestions for strengthening the vocational education ecosystem and facilitating greater participation of universities in the national skilling framework.

articles.full_content:
The Government has developed Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH), a Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for the skilling ecosystem under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). Launched on 13th September 2023, it brings the entire skilling ecosystem onto a single unified platform, integrating training, assessment, certification, employment and entrepreneurship services, while allowing training providers, employers and government schemes to onboard onto a common interoperable ecosystem. Built on a mobile-first approach and interoperable with other Government platforms such as National Career Service, eShram, DigiLocker and BHASHINI, SIDH advances the Government's vision of a unified, citizen-centric skilling ecosystem accessible to all.
As per Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) data, a total of 35,17,023 learners are registered under PMKVY 4.0, 52,98,397 under the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), 10,19,992under the Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS) scheme, and 4,96,755 under the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative. A total of 78,647 trainers holding a valid Trainer ID are registered on the platform. Further, 13,633 training centres are registered under PMKVY 4.0 (Short Term Training and Special Projects), 296 training centres under the JSS scheme, and 13,888 Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) are onboarded on SIDH. The key courses available on the platform span short-term skilling and apprenticeship programmes under PMKVY 4.0 and NAPS, community-based training under JSS, and foundational and applied Artificial Intelligence courses under SOAR. The number of youth registered, trained/oriented, certified and employed through the platform, State/UT wise, including in Punjab, Odisha and Chhattisgarh, particularly Nabarangpur and Bastar Lok Sabha Constituencies, is given at Annexure-A .
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), through the National Council for Vocational Education and Training (NCVET), has launched the Skilling for AI Readiness (SOAR) initiative to equip learners, educators and the workforce with foundational Artificial Intelligence (AI) knowledge and practical competencies. The initiative comprises nationally recognised, NSQF-aligned, fully online and self-paced AI courses delivered through the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) by NCVET-recognised Awarding Bodies. Subsequently, SOAR has been expanded beyond foundational AI literacy to include AI and AI application-oriented courses focused on AI for jobs, workplace productivity, sector-specific applications, inclusivity, and contextualised AI applications for the informal sector. As on 22.07.2026, a total of 4,96,426 learners have enrolled and 98,576 learners have been certified under the SOAR courses available on the Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH).

The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future ready, equipped with industry relevant skills.
The Government is actively promoting skill development in the space and geospatial emerging technology sectors through flagship schemes of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), namely the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS), which impart short-term skilling, up-skilling, re-skilling through Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL), and structured on-the-job apprenticeship training in areas such as GIS, spatial data management, drone technology, software development, telecommunications, and electronics. Furthermore, to strengthen the capacity of Non-Government Entities (NGEs) and academia, IN-SPACe under the Department of Space has introduced 11 short-term skill development courses in space technology, under which over 1,000 candidates have been successfully trained across the country.
The State/UT-wise number of candidates trained and apprentices engaged in space and geospatial related sectors during the last three years as well as the number of training centres/establishments under PMKVY and NAPS are provided at Annexure-I and Annexure-II respectively. The details of HEIs conducting various space technology courses across the country are given at Annexure-III .

Government skill programmes are then designed to bridge these identified skill gaps across sectors. The Sector Skill Councils (SSCs), led by industry experts, regularly conduct skill gap studies to assess sector-wise skill needs and set competency standards, which guide government interventions to align the workforce with industry requirements. Additionally, the SANKALP (Skill Acquisition and Knowledge Awareness for Livelihood Promotion)-supported National Skill Gap Study by National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) provides a standardized, data-driven framework to assess skill gaps across seven high-growth sectors. It helps MSDE align skilling initiatives with industry demand and future workforce needs. Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills including emerging technologies.
PMKVY 4.0 implemented since FY 2022-23 gives special emphasis on future skills and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning, Robotics, Cloud Computing, Internet of Things (IoT), Data Analytics, Cyber Security and Green Technologies, to prepare youth for new and emerging job roles.
The Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship (MSDE), has developed 170 NSQF-compliant courses, including 32 new-age/Future Skills courses under the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS), in emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, Industrial Robotics, Cyber Security, and Green Skills, etc. These courses are designed to equip youth across the country with industry-relevant skills in emerging technologies, enhance their employability, and meet the evolving demand for skilled manpower across various sectors. These courses are delivered through a nationwide network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs).
The number of candidates trained under Artificial Intelligence and other emerging technology-related skilling programmes, year and State/UT-wise, is at Annexure .
Under PMKVY 1.0 to PMKVY 3.0, which were implemented during FY-2015-16 to FY 2021-23, a total of 1.11 Crore candidates were certified, out of which 24.38 lakhs were reported placed under the Short Term Training (STT) component of the scheme. Further, under PMKVY 4.0, the focus is to empower the trained candidates to choose their varied career paths, and they are suitably oriented for the same. Hence, placements are not monitored under PMKVY 4.0.
Skill Gap studies are conducted from time to time to assess the industry demand and the employability of the candidates trained under various Skill India initiatives in various sectors. Such studies guide the interventions of the Government aimed at preparing the workforce as per the industry needs. Sector Skill Councils (SSCs) have undertaken skill gap studies across sectors such as Electronics, Logistics, Advance Manufacturing, etc. providing demand–supply assessments and manpower projections.

articles.title: PROMOTION OF SKILL DEVELOPMENT IN THE MARITIME SECTOR
articles.full_content:
Under the Government of India’s Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) delivers skill, re-skill and up- skill training through an extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under various schemes, viz. Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs), to all the sections of the society across the country including Kasaragod. The SIM aims at enabling youth of India to get future-ready, equipped with industry-relevant skills, including for the maritime sector.
Some of the initiatives taken to promote skilling in the maritime sector include:
• Under PMKVY, training is imparted in logistics and maritime-related job roles such as Documentation Assistant, Consignment Booking Assistant, Consignment Tracking Executive, Courier Delivery Executive, Signalman Port Operation, Vessel Operator Grade-1, Marine Capture Fisherman and Protective & Marine Painter, among others. In Kasaragod district of Kerala, 240 candidates have been trained/oriented under PMKVY, out of which 197 candidates are certified.
• The Directorate General of Shipping (DGS) has approved 171 Maritime Training Institutes (MTIs) in India. The employment of seafarers on Indian or Foreign Ships depends on their training, assessment and certification in accordance with the International Convention on Standards of Training, Certification and Watchkeeping (STCW Convention) of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) for the seafarers, to which India is a signatory.
• The DGS has also issued a list of approved maritime training courses. All these courses are to be in line with the Model Course issued by the IMO and the STCW Convention, 2010. The Training, Examination and Assessment Programme (TEAP) manual has also been issued by the DGS, providing necessary guidelines and details of the training courses, seagoing services and examination. Besides these, there is a common course for faculties of the Maritime Training Institutes (MTIs), namely Vertical Integration Course for Trainers.
• Additionally, the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (MoPSW) has initiated various steps for promoting skill development, including for coastal youth in the ports, shipping, and waterways sector by strengthening maritime education and training, upgrading the curriculum of maritime institutes, and enhancing industry-oriented skill programmes in the port sector and logistics.
